decision.reason: Both retained timing floors and reported electrical limits pass. Five timed-net reserve shortfalls, nonzero congestion and exploratory area overage remain. The prior candidate has lower congestion and area but negative hold.
decision.next_gate: Diagnose and reduce the 25 reconciled Metal3 congestion markers and five reserve shortfalls while preserving both timing floors, all protected cells and SRAM write paths. Compare against this timing reference and retain the lower-congestion predecessor.

phase_effects.native_counter_caveat: Journal rollback resets the optimizer counter; independently reread additions are authoritative.
phase_effects.association_boundary: Native net/marker association is not causal attribution; initial route already had 25 overflow units.

result.boundary: Native marker demand reconciles with this saved whole-chip grid and flow total. Crossing attribution is distinct from guide-area overlap and does not prove one net caused the shared overflow.

minimum_pin_access.boundary: Minimum-one-access-point probe. Initial grid warnings are separate from final no-access counts; this does not establish simultaneous routability.

evidence_boundary: Global-route estimates only; retained fast-cell -40C / SRAM -55C mismatch remains.
The first reroute preserves cells and placement but changes timing/electrical checks and already has 25 overflow; repair gains are measured separately.
1,790 constant ties have no reported timing limits and are not counted as timed-net passes; input-driven and clock nets are outside the cell-driven inventory.
Actual netlist/geometry readback counts 90 delay cells and six buffers; native journal progress counters undercount accepted additions.
No new Lean theorem, RTL change, extra pipeline cycle, complete compiler/package refinement, detailed routing, extraction or backend promotion.
